customManagers.description: ARG BAIKAL_VERSION and the ARG BAIKAL_SHA256 beneath it, captured together so one PR moves both. The dockerfile manager only reads an ARG that a FROM expands, and these feed a release URL and its checksum. github-release-attachments finds the release asset whose SHA-256 is the pinned one, then downloads the same-named asset of the new release and hashes it, so no checksum is ever set by hand. The two ARGs must stay adjacent and in this order.
ARG PHP_VERSION, which build-static.sh would otherwise resolve to the newest 8.5 at build time. php-src tags releases as php-8.5.11.
ARG CADDY_VERSION, which xcaddy would otherwise resolve to the newest Caddy at build time.
ARG CBROTLI_VERSION, which xcaddy would otherwise resolve to the newest plugin at build time.
ARG MERCURE_VERSION, which xcaddy would otherwise resolve to the newest plugin at build time.
ARG VULCAIN_VERSION, which xcaddy would otherwise resolve to the newest plugin at build time.

packageRules.description: Subject prefix for the image's build inputs. Kernel style, 'subsystem: short description', because these are commits on main like any other.
Subject prefix for the binary's pinned roots, which are build inputs too.

One PR for the builder, Caddy and its plugins. A FrankenPHP release can require a newer Caddy or plugin, and test/pinned-versions.sh fails any build whose binary disagrees with a pin, so moving one without the others goes red.
Subject prefix for the Baikal release.
Subject prefix for the local toolchain: mise.toml and the composer-pinned PHPStan.
Subject prefix for the workflows' action pins and the Renovate image itself.

jq tags releases as jq-1.8.2. mise strips that prefix from aqua's registry entry; Renovate does not read the aqua registry, so without this every candidate version is discarded as unparseable and no PR is ever raised.

Never propose a new hash for a Baikal version already pinned. An archive swapped under the same version is a supply-chain alarm, not an update, and the daily canary's sha256sum -c goes red on it instead.

prBodyNotes: Every statement in `baikal.openvex.json` is scoped to the exact version of the component it was argued against. A builder that ships a different version makes that statement stop matching, and `just scan` goes red. Re-argue reachability against the version this build ships and update the statement, or delete it — widening the version to clear the finding asserts something nobody checked.

The acceptance suite asserts the binary carries no file capability. Upstream's own FrankenPHP builds set `cap_net_bind_service=ep`, and a binary with a file capability cannot be exec'd at all under `--cap-drop ALL`.
